decision: KEEP TypeScript/native Fetch and AbortSignal; FIX the admitted session cleanup scope to include observer setup.
constraints: Node and browser-hosted read-only client with synchronous display callbacks and native abort/timer APIs.
A validated remote handle must reach best-effort deletion if local setup fails; fixed errors must not copy host exception details.
No extra runtime dependency, retry, history or new wire contract. Existing display-callback error identity and independent deletion timeout remain intact.

alternatives.assessment: Selected: explicit resource scope covers the validated handle, partially allocated controller/timer, final withdrawal and DELETE. Static optional-resource types expose partial setup; runtime negative tests verify it. No runtime wrapper or FFI is needed.
Can express the same try-finally and host APIs. Removing static TypeScript syntax would not change the cleanup scope or strengthen runtime admission; no runtime advantage demonstrated.

Official documentation supports JavaScript environments and ESM/CommonJS interop. Shared JVM implementation can be valuable, but this component has no JVM ownership requirement. It still depends on host Fetch/timers and explicit remote-handle lifetime; no material win established.

alternatives.technology: Rust / WebAssembly with web-sys and wasm-bindgen
alternatives.assessment: Official Fetch example wraps host requests and promises through JsFuture. Native ownership is useful for native resources, but does not independently delete a server handle across asynchronous host setup failure. This small host orchestration adds no native compute workload justifying an FFI deployment boundary.

limits: Host-failure injection is not a browser compatibility or physical fault qualification.
Cleanup remains best effort and relies on working host cancellation, timeout and fetch APIs. No asynchronous DELETE guarantee on process loss.
No language performance comparison was executed; KEEP follows the narrow resource-lifetime and interoperability requirements.
No changed timing/byte thresholds, credentials storage, actuation, targeting or security/availability certification.
